profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Red Oak, Texas data center campus, the company's second in Ellis County after its original Midlothian site opened in 2019. Google announced the Red Oak project in 2023, describing a site at 156 N. Austin Boulevard in Red Oak spanning roughly 285,000 square feet, with more than $600 million in planned investment including an initial $330 million in the project's first year and construction expected to take about two years. Google said the completed facility would support 30 permanent full time positions, while construction itself generated nearly 1,200 temporary jobs, and framed the project as serving growing demand for its cloud, Workspace, and Maps services. The Ellis County Press reported the Red Oak campus's first building became operational by late 2025. This particular OSM mapped building sits on North State Highway 342 rather than the N. Austin Boulevard address Google has given for the campus overall, which likely reflects a different building or access point on the same Red Oak site rather than a separate project, since Google's own Ellis County location page does not break out individual building addresses or power capacity.

On September 2, 2026, Google folded continued Red Oak buildout into a broader $40 billion Texas investment announcement running through 2027, which also includes a fourth building at the nearby Midlothian campus valued at nearly $1 billion. Google's own materials describe that statewide commitment as supporting cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure and cite $55.7 billion in economic activity the company says its Texas operations generated in 2025, alongside newer Google data center or energy announcements in Armstrong County, Haskell County, Wilbarger County, and a combined energy center spanning Gray and Roberts counties, all disclosed in 2025 and 2026 as part of the same statewide push. Google has described its Texas data center footprint, including Ellis County, as anchoring three AI focused hubs across the state, though it has not published building level megawatt figures for any individual Ellis County structure that this research could confirm.

Ercot, the grid operator for most of Texas, has flagged data center and large load interconnection requests concentrated in North Texas corridors like Ellis County as a major driver behind its 2026 long term load forecasts, prompting the Public Utility Commission of Texas to adopt new large load interconnection study procedures governing how quickly hyperscale campuses such as Google's Midlothian and Red Oak sites can add grid capacity. Ellis County's own economic development materials have cited the Red Oak and Midlothian projects together as the county's largest capital investment in its history, ahead of any manufacturing or logistics project it had previously recruited.

reading.body:
The Red Oak campus is Google's second data center site in Ellis County, Texas, with its first building operational by late 2025. Google announced the project in 2023 and committed $600 million initially, with the site planned to span roughly 285,000 square feet and support 30 permanent positions. The company folded continued Red Oak buildout into a $40 billion Texas investment through 2027 announced on September 2, 2026, positioning it as one of three AI-focused data center hubs the company is developing across the state. Google does not publish individual building or campus power specifications.

An aggregator-sourced figure of approximately 86 megawatts circulates for this campus, but Google has not confirmed it directly in published specifications. If that figure is accurate, it would represent roughly 2,150 racks at an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack, a typical density for AI training workloads. No published megawatt figure for Red Oak appears in Google's own disclosure, making its actual power draw unknown and its ranking among Texas data centers unmeasurable against operator-confirmed data.

The Ercot grid operator flagged data center interconnection requests in North Texas corridors including Ellis County as a major driver of its 2026 load forecasts, prompting the Texas Public Utility Commission to adopt new large-load interconnection study procedures to manage hyperscale campus additions. Ellis County economic development materials cited the Red Oak and Midlothian projects together as the county's largest capital investment in its history. Google's Texas strategy now centers on three AI data center hubs, making Ellis County's grid capacity and interconnection timeline a binding variable in the company's ability to sustain the buildout rate it has committed to through 2027.
